repo_model.summary: This repository is a RelBench generic-search starter workspace. The root candidate loads an environment-selected task and writes trivial task-specific validation/test predictions, while the bundled helpers and immutable evaluator define the data, scoring, and archiving workflow.

entrypoints.how_to_run: From the repository root, run `python main.py --debug` for the cheap contract mode or `python main.py` for the full run; the RelBench and output environment variables must be set.
With evaluator environment variables set, run `python kapso_evaluation/grader.py --fidelity fast|full [--fraction F] [--seed S]`.

where_to_edit.role: Primary candidate implementation; replace the trivial task-type branches with feature construction, training, and prediction logic.
Reusable task-loading, prediction-saving, temporal-safety, and MAP@K utilities.
Reference for required run modes, artifact names, shapes, leakage rules, and prediction semantics.

claims.statement: The candidate loads RELBENCH_DATASET and RELBENCH_TASK, obtains the RelBench task with download=False, determines validation/test row counts from task tables, and writes artifacts under KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR.

evidence.description: Reads the dataset name from the environment
Reads the task name from the environment

claims.statement: The seeded baseline dispatches by task type: recommendations use tiled destination ids 0 through K-1, binary classification uses 0.5, multiclass classification uses uniform 1/C scores, and other tasks use the training-target median.

evidence.description: Tiles the ranking across validation rows
Computes the training-target median for other tasks

claims.statement: kapso_datasets.common provides a TaskContext containing the dataset, task, database, and train/validation/test tables, plus centralized prediction saving and utility checks.

evidence.description: Loads task context from the sanitized cache

claims.statement: The grader is the scoring boundary: it runs main.py in an isolated child process, loads prediction artifacts, validates their basic contract, evaluates the validation table with RelBench, and selects the configured primary metric.

evidence.description: Starts the candidate in a subprocess

claims.statement: Full-fidelity evaluations archive prediction files, validation metrics, selection labels, an evaluator-tree snapshot, and a filtered copy of candidate code; fast evaluations are treated as pipeline checks and are not archived.

evidence.description: Begins copying candidate code for audit

claims.statement: For normal evaluations, both val_predictions.npy and test_predictions.npy must exist after every run and must be positionally aligned with the corresponding RelBench task tables; validation predictions must come from a model that did not train on validation labels.

evidence.description: Requires both prediction files after every run
Requires validation predictions to be out-of-sample
Forbids using validation labels in the validation model

claims.statement: Prediction formats are task-specific: binary and regression use float vectors of length N, binary values must be probabilities in [0,1], multiclass uses float scores shaped (N,C), and recommendation uses integer (N,K) ranked distinct destination ids in range.

evidence.description: Defines binary and regression output formats
Requires recommendation ids to be ranked, distinct, and in range

claims.statement: Candidate data access must use the sanitized RelBench cache with download=False; test labels are physically absent and must not be probed.

evidence.description: Defines the official validation metric as the search score
Requires the RelBench API with download=False
States that test labels are absent

claims.statement: The score of record is the configured official validation primary metric; test predictions are collected as artifacts but cannot be scored inside this sanitized evaluation loop.

evidence.description: Defines the manifest score as the validation primary metric
States that test predictions cannot be scored in the loop
Places the primary validation metric in the manifest score

claims.statement: When temporal features are built with the starter helper, every feature row must have its time column at or before the seed time; violations raise RuntimeError.

evidence.description: Detects rows after the seed time

claims.statement: The required quick validation is `python main.py --debug`, followed by the full `python main.py` run; the harness validates and scores both runs.

evidence.description: States that the harness runs the program twice

claims.statement: After producing predictions, `python kapso_datasets/check_predictions.py` can pre-validate file existence, shapes, finite values, binary bounds, and recommendation warnings.
A successful official evaluation prints the validation metrics and a KAPSO_EVAL_MANIFEST line containing the score of record and run metadata.

evidence.description: Stores the primary metric as the score

claims.statement: In rolling evaluation, an absent or empty val.parquet makes the candidate treat the invocation as a rolling tick and suppress val_predictions.npy; the rolling grader instead collects per-tick test predictions and assembles final vectors by official indices.

evidence.description: Documents empty validation tables in rolling snapshots
Uses zero validation rows when the path is absent or empty
Suppresses validation output in rolling mode

claims.statement: The seeded baseline does not implement a cheaper debug algorithm: --debug is only consulted when formatting its final log message, so prediction generation is otherwise the same.

evidence.description: Prediction generation begins without a debug branch
Debug status is included in the output message

claims.statement: load_task defaults to upto_test_timestamp=True; autocomplete callers that need post-test-cutoff entity rows as inputs must explicitly pass False.

evidence.description: Shows the default timestamp cutoff argument
Applies the timestamp cutoff when obtaining the database

claims.statement: The local prediction checker warns rather than fails when recommendation ids are out of range or duplicated, so an OK result does not guarantee a semantically valid distinct ranking.

evidence.description: Warns on recommendation ids outside the destination range
Warns when duplicate ids are present
Defines valid recommendation ids as ranked and distinct

claims.statement: The runtime requires Python with relbench and numpy installed; the candidate directly imports NumPy and RelBench task APIs.

evidence.description: Lists Python, relbench, and numpy as the required setup

claims.statement: The evaluator supplies environment configuration for dataset/task identity, primary metric, archive and cache locations, timeouts, and shared candidate caching; the baseline additionally reads the cache and run-output variables directly.

evidence.description: Lists dataset, task, and primary metric variables

book.summary: This repository is a RelBench generic-search starter workspace. The root candidate loads an environment-selected task and writes trivial task-specific validation/test predictions, while the bundled helpers and immutable evaluator define the data, scoring, and archiving workflow.

toc.title: Architecture
toc.one_liner: Task loading, prediction generation, contract helpers, and isolated evaluation are separated into the candidate, starter kit, and evaluator.

toc.title: Entrypoints
toc.one_liner: Run the root candidate directly or invoke the provided evaluator with the required environment.

toc.title: Where to edit
toc.one_liner: Replace the baseline logic in main.py and reuse the starter-kit contract helpers.

toc.title: Invariants
toc.one_liner: Prediction artifacts, leakage boundaries, and scoring semantics are fixed by the evaluation contract.

toc.title: Testing
toc.one_liner: Use the debug evaluator and prediction checker before relying on official validation scores.

toc.title: Gotchas
toc.one_liner: Rolling snapshots, debug mode, semantic recommendation checks, and autocomplete timestamps have non-obvious behavior.

toc.title: Dependencies
toc.one_liner: The workspace depends on Python with RelBench and NumPy, and receives task/evaluation configuration through environment variables.
